answer: Reputation-Weighted Action Delay. Each new identity must forge a public action history before its votes or payouts count; actions are verified against operator-controlled infrastructure logs. A cheap new wallet can whisper requests but cannot vote until its operator’s cluster reaches a minimum diversity score. A falcon flag marks clusters sharing operators, freezing all their identities’ rewards for 30 days. Attacker cost: one operator must run many distinct, costly infrastructure footprints per identity, so each extra sybil adds real hosting and compliance overhead.
